chunks.text: Neural networks are models made of layers, weights, and activation functions. They learn patterns from data and produce predictions.
A feedforward neural network passes input values forward through hidden layers to create an output. It does not use cycles.
Backpropagation computes gradients of the loss function and updates weights so that the model prediction becomes closer to the target.
Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training data and performs poorly on unseen validation or test data.
Regularization methods such as dropout and weight decay reduce overfitting by limiting model complexity.
Convolutional neural networks use filters to detect local visual patterns such as edges, textures, and shapes in images.
Recurrent neural networks process sequential data by carrying hidden state across time steps.
Attention mechanisms allow a model to focus on the most relevant tokens when producing a representation or prediction.
